journey_note: Task navigation for existing products, data and interfaces. These are not additional SKUs, completed workflows or new authority. The catalogue edition dates the packaging, not the underlying observations.

journeys.title: Inspect generated measurements
journeys.summary: Choose an instrument, inspect its dated run and retrieve the supporting record.
journeys.input: A named model, endpoint or other supported subject and the question to examine.
journeys.output: A scoped result with method, observation date, evidence references and explicit unknowns.
steps: Select the applicable axis and subject.
Read the sample unit, method and original observation time.
Open the supporting artifact and retain its exact identifier.
journeys.boundary: A published slot is not a completed run. This view does not start a fresh measurement.
journeys.recovery: Keep the original record and its source/version; use Verify for supported signed records.

journeys.title: Verify and keep a record
journeys.summary: Check a supported record without turning a signature into a safety claim.
journeys.input: The exact supported card or evidence packet and its expected subject.
journeys.output: A verification result that separates valid, invalid and uncheckable conditions.
steps: Select the original record, not a screenshot of its verdict.
Inspect the supported signature, identity and inclusion checks.
Retain the original bytes, record identifier and verification scope.
journeys.boundary: Integrity is not truth, current authority, certification or evidence that a payment occurred.
journeys.recovery: Keep the original bytes. On an unsupported format or failed read, preserve UNCHECKABLE instead of calling it false.

journeys.title: Inspect changes and corrections
journeys.summary: Follow a claim over time without silently rewriting its earlier evidence.
journeys.input: A claim, subject or source identifier and the versions being compared.
journeys.output: Available change, withdrawal, unavailable-source and correction records.
steps: Locate the relevant published source or claim.
Compare its original and subsequent records and their dates.
Inspect the existing correction or recheck status.
journeys.boundary: A new report date does not prove a new source read. Source reachability is not a verified incident.
journeys.recovery: Preserve predecessor and successor references; distinguish unresolved reads from confirmed changes.

journeys.title: Learn from evidence
journeys.summary: Practise interpreting a record before preparing a human-review draft.
journeys.input: An applicable axis and its loaded, dated source record.
journeys.output: Source-linked practice and a local proposal draft with its limitations.
steps: Inspect the source date, status and unknowns.
Complete a practice question and inspect the explanation.
Save a source-bound draft or return to the original evidence.
journeys.boundary: Practice, points and draft completeness do not establish professional competence or grant authority.
journeys.recovery: Keep source pins and local work. Failed refreshes must not be treated as new evidence.

journeys.title: Use GSPC in an AI host
journeys.summary: Bring the existing evidence reader into a supported tool or use the browser fallback.
journeys.input: A compatible host and permission to enable the integration in that workspace.
journeys.output: The documented read-only evidence interface; installed-host results remain separately qualified.
steps: Choose the documented host or free MCP reader.
Read a named subject and inspect the evidence returned.
Retain the result, then disconnect or revoke access through the host.
journeys.boundary: A listing or tool manifest is not an installation, universal platform support or authority to execute.
journeys.recovery: Use the public verifier when the host is unavailable. Preserve evidence IDs rather than copying only summaries.

journeys.title: Prepare a human review
journeys.summary: Make the proposal and missing evidence understandable to the responsible person.
journeys.input: An exact source-bound proposal, intended purpose and reviewer role.
journeys.output: A draft and, only where actually recorded, a separate reviewer disposition.
steps: Inspect the subject, arguments, destination and evidence revision.
Check the real reviewer role and the service limitations.
Keep the actual disposition distinct from any permitted execution and observed effect.
journeys.boundary: An operator label, shared token, practice answer or machine signature is not proof of an authenticated human decision.
journeys.recovery: Keep HOLD or UNKNOWN where identity, authority, storage or an effect has not been established.

journeys.title: Reuse a published dataset
journeys.summary: Find the data version and its reuse terms before incorporating it into another workflow.
journeys.input: A named dataset, intended purpose and required period or version.
journeys.output: The published data and provenance, or an explicit access/licensing enquiry where required.
steps: Select the exact component and published revision.
Check code, data and model rights separately.
Retain the source, version, attribution and correction references.
journeys.boundary: Public visibility is not blanket commercial or training permission; private customer data is not included.
journeys.recovery: Keep the permitted artifact and its digest. Use the existing enquiry route for rights or delivery questions.

journeys.title: Inspect a sector evidence pack
journeys.summary: Examine what a particular test observed without turning a mapping into a compliance verdict.
journeys.input: The relevant system, use case, jurisdiction and provision or technical question.
journeys.output: Published observations, applicable method references and unresolved coverage.
steps: Read what the pack actually tests.
Inspect the original sample, method, evidence and date.
Keep technical findings separate from the responsible professional review.
journeys.boundary: A technical marking check is not certification, insurance cover, legal advice or a whole-law assessment.
journeys.recovery: Preserve the tested source/version; use the current coverage map to see untested and hash-only entries.

journeys.title: Request a defined deliverable
journeys.summary: Use the existing commission or enquiry path for the output you actually need.
journeys.input: A named subject, optional applicable axis, intended use and requested output.
journeys.output: A request-attestation receipt and on-file evidence where supported; fresh work needs its own agreed scope.
steps: Check whether the route supplies existing evidence or new work.
Review the actual terms for that exact request.
Retain the request, receipt, delivered artifact and recovery status separately.
journeys.boundary: A payment challenge or receipt does not prove a fresh run, completed delivery or recipient acceptance. No automatic second payment on an unknown result.
journeys.recovery: Recover the original result through the supported account/receipt path. An unresolved outcome requires reconciliation, not a new purchase.

journeys.title: Explore simulations and practice
journeys.summary: Use the existing arena without confusing a game result with a measurement.
journeys.input: A selected published practice task or simulation with its stated rules.
journeys.output: Local practice feedback or a labelled simulated outcome.
steps: Read the task, rules and historical-reference limits.
Run only the supported local practice activity.
Inspect the feedback and the underlying evidence separately.
journeys.boundary: Synthetic opponents, local points and replay are not model calls, training admission, human competence or compliance.
journeys.recovery: Retain permitted local outputs where offered. Use the canonical board for admitted measurements.
